chunks: They left early in the morning bent on this purpose.

key_terms.حَرْدٍ: Haste, urgency, or speed in movement
key_terms.قَادِرِينَ: Capable, having the power or capacity (to bear load)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'on hard' mean in Surah Al-Hashr regarding the Banu al-Nadir?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Banu al-Nadir's expulsion, illustrating the transient nature of worldly wealth when divorced from divine favor. The term 'qadirin' (capable/able) emphasizes their physical capacity to carry their treasures, yet their haste ('hard') signifies the urgency of their departure from the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) authority. This event serves as a historical precedent for the removal of the Jewish tribes from Medina, reinforcing the concept of divine justice in territorial and communal shifts.
